newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico approaching oversupply of soy meal - ASA/USB.
newsitem.headline: Mexico approaching oversupply of soy meal - ASA/USB.

text.p: Soy crushers in Mexico have said soybean meal sales are down and that they may soon have an excess of supply, the Mexican office of the American Soy Association and the United Soybean Board said.
"Crushers are stockpiling meal and some of the large crushers have reduced production volumes because of this fact," the groups said in a recent report.
Local soybean prices are at about 2,600 pesos ($331) per metric ton, it added.
With the new Cargill crusher in Mexico, the report said there is more supply of meal than demand.

"The livestock industry is showing signs of increasing populations on feed, but livestock numbers are not growing at a rate fast enough to keep up with the rate of crush in the oil industry," the report said.
The report also said that seasonal soybean tariffs will enter into effect in September for North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) countries, and in August for non-NAFTA nations.
